A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POATE research. Their text, tables, figures, algorithm and Appendices A–E are readable and matchable despite added material and layout changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original attack-success experiments, defense evaluations, model-size comparisons and appendix error analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds hybrid-attack results, harmfulness evaluations, defense timings and further defense comparisons.

M1.justification: The core POATE algorithm and both CoT defenses remain unchanged. v4 introduces a supplementary POATE + GCG variant that appends GCG-optimized adversarial suffixes to POATE prompts, constituting a limited procedural adaptation (Section 4.2; Appendix C.2).

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate harmful-query jailbreaking on AdvBench, unsafe XSTest examples and MaliciousInstructions. The additions introduce no new dataset, domain or task requirement; runtime measurements concern the retained defenses.

E2.justification: v3 Tables 12–13 compare the CoT defenses with no defense. Their v4 counterparts, Tables 15–16, add SmoothLLM across the same seven attacks on Llama-3.1 and Gemma-2. SmoothLLM already appeared against POATE in Table 3, but its participation in these comparisons is new.

E3.justification: v4 adds harmfulness scoring of manually extracted harmful outputs using 10 samples per dataset for two models (Appendix A.7), plus a 50-query defense-timing protocol on an RTX A6000 using vLLM (Appendix B). The original 50-per-dataset ASR evaluation and human/GPT-4 judging procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds POATE + GCG composition and defense-runtime analyses, and extends the existing harmfulness-grading diagnostic with scores on isolated harmful outputs. The earlier few-shot, template, scaling, intention-shift and human-written-prompt analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain seed 42 in Appendix A.6 and the same aggregate reporting practices. v4 adds no repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 are unchanged. New Table 14 reports hybrid ASRs of 20/24/30% on AdvBench/XSTest/MI, versus 12/2/18% for GCG and 72/54/76% for POATE. Additional results include extracted-output harmfulness means near 4.4 for Llama-3.1 and 4.0 for GPT-4o, defense timings of 24–43 seconds per 50 queries, and SmoothLLM results (Tables 11–12, 15–16). The new harmfulness scores use a different protocol from retained Table 10.

T1.justification: Appendix B newly defines total prompt length as n = P + D, assumes a small constant defense length D, and asserts O(n) decoder-only inference to argue limited overhead. v3 contains no corresponding complexity argument. No formal proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims about POATE, larger-model vulnerability and the two CoT defenses. The supplementary experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v4 attributes hybrid underperformance to adversarial-suffix detectability, interprets lower extracted-output harmfulness as stronger residual GPT-4o safeguards, and argues that the defenses have practical runtime overhead. The stated limitations concerning intention shifts, single-turn attacks and untested closed models remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds hardware, software and timing information for the new defense-runtime experiment, while retaining the earlier H100 infrastructure and generation settings. Footnote 1 changes the documented code repository pointer from arxiv2025-poate-attack to emnlp2025-poate-attack; availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work review are unchanged. However, Section 4.2 and new Appendix C.2 additionally position POATE as an augmentation to the established GCG attack, extending its previous positioning as a standalone competing attack.

P1.justification: v4 expands the experimental discussion, rewrites portions of Appendices B and E, clarifies captions and changes appendix-reference formatting. New Appendix C.2 shifts the retained scaling discussion to C.3. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely stable.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 11, 12 and 14 and expands the former defense tables with SmoothLLM rows, now Tables 15–16. Existing diagrams, plots and examples are retained, with some resizing, repositioning and page reflow within the same two-column layout.

improvement.justification: The added SmoothLLM comparisons, hybrid-attack test and extracted-output harmfulness analysis modestly strengthen empirical completeness while preserving the core evidence. The gains are limited: harmfulness scoring uses small manually processed subsets, and Appendix B's deployment argument exceeds what its uncontrolled timing measurements and unproved O(n) assertion establish. These weaknesses temper the useful additional validation.
